reviews.title: I was there!!
reviews.body: One of my college roommates and I hitched from Oxford, Ohio to Watkins Glen to be part of this amazing and historic event. We arrived on Wednesday afternoon, and amazingly, our last ride was about 35 miles from WG, from a girl who actually lived a few blocks from us in Oxford who was going there as well! Anyway, it was a great time. It was also a trying experience since we were not expecting to be part of one of the largest cities in the country at the time, but the situation called for us to forge on. With the help of the entrepreneurs that were selling anything you could want, we got through the tough stuff. We went into the concert area early on Friday and established our "spot" about 60 yards back from the stage, nearly in the center. But here's where what I remember that differs from what I've read: The Band came out on Friday (disguised as a soundcheck) after the Dead and the Allmans played forEVER and played their asses off. With much anticipation, I waited. Here's what I remember... they played half of WS Walcott's Medicine Show and walked off the stage. That was IT -- DONE -- FINITO! Less than three minutes of total performance time and they were done. Dead logged at least two hours. Allmans played nearly the same amount of time. The Band... about 2:30 and they were done. PISSED ME OFF! But not as much as that album they CALL live at Watkins Glen. Sorry guys.. that was NOT recorded at WG. But I digress... It was an amazing experience and I honestly remember nearly every bit of the trip hitching TO the show, and not a bit of the trip back to Oxford. Good music is magic... and wears you OUT! Thanks to all involved for putting this up there for the rest of us to enjoy! If you were there, you know...

reviews.title: Mountain Jam
reviews.body: I read recently that Butch Trucks said he thought that the encore was a disaster, particularly mentioning the Mountain Jam. He said this was so because the drugs didn't mix well ("The Bad was drunk, Dead tripping, and Allman Bros. coked out.") I've listened to this a few times, and completely disagree. WHile there is plenty more to the show - namely the China>Rider, Playin', and Eyes - as an ABB fan, the Mountain Jam is what caught my eye first, and I think that Trucks in crazy. While I may understand where he's coming from, as it sounds like the Dead's take on the Mountain Jam, not necessarily the same thing as the famed ABB version from the Fillmore East in 1971, it is nonetheless DOPE. I would highly recommend that anyone who likes the Allman Bros. and the Dead go listen to this, but first listen to the DS>Spanish Jam>Lovelight from 2/11/70

reviews.title: The Bus came by , we all got on !
reviews.body: The big blue bus (35 ft 1957 gmc school bus) drove thru the neighborhood and took anyone who was left on Love's Corner---headed north from philly to one of the best concerts ever---got there early enough to get pretty close to the race track---found some blotter---wondered thru a sea of humanity (600,000 they say) and floated on the vibes and the music into the wee hours--the next morning when everyone was leaving ---we were in so close that we had to wait till the road opened up to drive---we watched a river of brothers and sisters --as wide as the road , flow by us for 12 straight hours--almost everyone made it back to the bus and we headed back to face down the Rizzo Gestapo regime as best we could---like Ken said "you're either on the bus or you're off the bus"

reviews.title: I’m telling you
reviews.body: First off I’m biased every show on Archive.org is an incredible gift. Yes there was a time when l might have thought that a show the Grateful Dead preformed was below par. However today fifty three years after this show this is now the best show ever. I dare any reviewer from past reviews that put this show down or any other show down to write the same put down today 7/28/25 or beyond. Every show they did is really good. Yeah maybe I can say how many times did you guys get on stage and do it 30 years with everything else that involves. Go ahead say it.yea I’m biased. The Grateful Dead were and still are unsurpassed in quality and sonic experience and tribal experience for thirty years they did it and beyond. That’s my story I’m sticking to it.

reviews.title: It Wasn't Woodstock but....
reviews.body: it was the next best thing. Heard about Summer Jam as I was hitching to Montreal, July '73. Arrived there and camped out on Mount Blanc and then next day headed back down and stuck my thumb out for Watkins Glen! Arrived early in the morning and walked the five miles from town to the concert site, there were freaks everywhere! Tipped toed over numerous sleeping bodies to within 50 yards of the stage and woke up the next morning to Jerry's soulful guitar. The next few hours were filled with the most amazing live music I've ever heard. And yes, they all jammed at the end, is there a recording of it somewhere? All I know is that this is one of my most treasured memories. I think the 60's really ended at Watkins Glen that weekend ah me!......
